m.note.lock_chaos: {chaos} with a locked side: the number of new mods is assumed to follow the normal rare mod-count distribution (GGG has not published it).
m.note.bench_inferred: Approximate: bench craft eligibility is inferred from the base's defence types; the export has no spawn tags for bench crafts.
m.note.base_price: Base item price is not included.
m.note.aisling_remove: Aisling model assumes no existing mod is removed. If the real Research craft removes a random mod, the cost here is understated and the success chance overstated.
m.note.lower_essence: Lower-tier essences are not offered after fracturing: they require a Normal item.
m.note.essence_annul: Approximate: if the {annul} removes the essence mod, the plan counts it as a restart (the essence mod is not tracked as removable), so the cost is an upper bound.
m.obj.min_cost.label: lowest expected cost
m.obj.min_cost.desc: Minimise expected total cost in chaos: cost of one attempt / chance of success, plus recovery and bench (optional Divine Orbs for the numbers are shown separately).
m.obj.min_attempts.label: fewest currency applications
m.obj.min_attempts.desc: Minimise the expected number of currency / bench applications per finished item (each strategy is evaluated with its cost-optimal recovery policy).
m.obj.min_variance.label: lowest bad-luck cost
m.obj.min_variance.desc: Risk-averse: minimise the bad-luck cost = expected cost + 2 standard deviations of the total cost (recovery branches included), so a plan that is cheap on average but swingy loses to a steadier one.

m.rule.rare_mod_count_note: Commonly cited distribution for Chaos/Alchemy/Essence/Fossil rares (4:8/12, 5:3/12, 6:1/12). Not published by GGG.
m.rule.magic_mod_count_note: Alteration/Transmutation: 1 or 2 mods. 50/50 split is an assumption.
m.rule.fossil_note: Fossil tag weights are applied multiplicatively for every matching mod tag (weight/100). 0 blocks the tag.
m.rule.essence_note: Screaming, Shrieking, Deafening, corruption-only and off-ladder essences (e.g. Essence of Desolation) reforge a rare directly (their currency text: 'Upgrades a normal item to rare or reforges a rare item'); lower tiers only upgrade a normal item, so they need {scour} between attempts.
m.rule.harvest_note: Modelled as: first mod forced from the tag, remaining mods rolled like a {chaos}. The real Harvest reforge algorithm is not public.
m.rule.eldritch_note: Approximate: each Ember/Ichor is assumed to create exactly the tier named in its description (Lesser=T6, Greater=T5, Grand=T4, Exceptional=T3); the export has no currency-to-tier table. Crafting is assumed to happen without an Eldritch presence (presence-upgraded versions are not modelled).
m.rule.eldritch_conflict_note: tiers 2 (Exquisite) and 1 (Perfect) are reached with the {conflict}, whose odds are not in the game data; the planner offers it only as a range plan when the Exceptional (tier 3) version and a Lesser currency for the other side exist on this base.
m.rule.conflict_note: Game data: the {conflict} 'Unpredictably raise[s] the strength of one Searing Exarch or Eater of Worlds modifier on an item and lower[s] the strength of another'; 'Lesser modifiers that have their strength lowered will be removed'; it 'Can only be used on items that have both a Searing Exarch and an Eater of Worlds implicit'; 'The chance of raising or lowering a modifier depends on its relative strength' - no formula is given. Not in the data, assumed: one Orb raises or lowers by exactly one tier, and the raised value meets the threshold (part of the best case).
m.rule.influence_exalt_note: Approximate: the Exalt's odds assume both affix sides are open (the most conservative case; with one side full the real chance is higher), and the item level the currency calls 'high-level' is not in the game data.
m.rule.influence_restart_note: A failed influence Exalt leaves the item influenced (Scouring and Annulment remove modifiers, not influence), so the plan starts over on a fresh base. Base items are not priced anywhere in the planner. Not modelled: Annulment of the wrong influenced mod followed by regular Exalted Orbs on the influenced item.
m.rule.awakener_note: Approximate: the game data says the second item is 'reforged as a rare item with both influence types and new modifiers'; that one influenced modifier from each item is kept is the community-documented rule, not in the data. Each item is assumed to carry exactly one influenced modifier, so that modifier is the one kept.
m.rule.dominance_note: Orb of Dominance (formerly Maven's Orb) removes one influenced modifier and upgrades another, turning a highest-tier one into an Elevated modifier. Which modifier is removed or upgraded is not in the game data, so it is offered only as a range plan: ask for the Elevated modifier as a target, e.g. 'TEXT (Elevated Elder)'.
m.rule.dominance_data_note: Game data: the {dominance} 'Removes one Influenced Modifier from an item with at least two Influenced Modifiers and upgrades another Influenced Modifier'; only a highest-tier modifier becomes Elevated; it can be used on Body Armours, Boots, Gloves and Helmets. The item is not destroyed: a failure removes the target's base modifier, and the plan then redoes the preparation (an upper bound - re-adding just that modifier is not modelled). The link from the Elevated modifier to its base modifier is derived (same influence, side, group and stats); the highest tier is checked by its minimum value, so an overlapping lower tier would also pass.
m.rule.fracture_note: Approximate: the {fracturing} 'fractures a random modifier' on a rare with at least 4 modifiers; how that modifier is chosen is not in the game data, so every modifier on the item is assumed equally likely. The target's value is fixed with {divine}s before fracturing; whether a {divine} can change a fractured value later is not stated in the data and is assumed not to.
m.rule.fracture_restart_note: A wrong modifier fractured cannot be undone and the item cannot be fractured again ('Cannot be used on Influenced or Fractured items'), so the plan starts over on a fresh base (base price not included). Not modelled: continuing with the wrongly fractured modifier.
m.rule.beastcraft_missing: Not supported (missing recipe data): the game data export contains no Beastcrafting recipes - not which beasts a recipe needs, not its cost, not what it adds or rerolls. Some outcome modifiers exist in mods.json (the Aspect suffixes 'of Farrul', 'of Saqawal', 'of Fenumus', 'of Craiceann', with no spawn weights), but nothing links a recipe to them.
m.rule.veiled_options_note: Approximate: the game data lists the unveiled outcomes and their spawn weights, but not how the 3 unveil options are drawn. Assumed: 3 different outcomes of the veiled modifier's side, drawn by spawn weight without replacement, never sharing a mod group with a mod already on the item. Only the generic pool ('Chosen' / 'of the Order') is used; Syndicate-member outcomes (Catarina's, It's, Aisling's ...) are not offered.
m.rule.aisling_note: Approximate: Aisling's Research craft is not in the game data at all. Modelled as requested: it adds one veiled modifier to an item with a free affix slot, without removing a mod, and the veiled modifier takes the free slot kept on the target's side. If it instead removes a random modifier (like the Veiled Exalted Orb in the data), these numbers do not apply. Not offered as a helper (slot blocking): nothing in the data supports it.
m.rule.veiled_chaos_note: Approximate: the {veiled_chaos} 'Reforges a rare item with new random modifiers including a random Veiled modifier' (currency text) - the whole item is rerolled, nothing is kept. Not in the data, assumed: the veiled modifier is a prefix or a suffix with 50% each, and it counts toward the usual rare mod count (4-6).
m.rule.veiled_restart_note: A wrong unveil cannot be undone except by removing the mod; the planner compares restarting with {annul} retries (uniform over the explicit mods; a removed target restarts) and uses the cheaper.
m.rule.fracture_kept_note: The fractured modifier stays: Chaos, Fossil, Essence and Harvest rerolls, {scour} and {annul} never remove it.
m.eld.wrong_side: this is an {other} implicit ({cur}), not a {side} implicit
m.eld.no_family: no Eldritch implicit with this stat line exists in the game data

m.eld.class_none: {cls} cannot have Eldritch implicits: Embers and Ichors apply only to {classes} (currency description)
m.eld.influenced: influenced items cannot take Eldritch implicits (currency: 'Cannot be used on Shaper, Elder or Elderslayer influenced items')
m.eld.not_on_class: this {side} implicit does not roll on {cls} (its spawn weights allow other item classes: {classes})
m.eld.ilvl: Eldritch implicits require item level {lvl} (required_level in the game data); base is {ilvl}
m.eld.needs_tier: needs tier {tier} or better, but Embers/Ichors only create tiers 6-3; {note}
m.eld.below: the highest Eldritch tier reaches {top:g}, below the threshold
m.eld.label: {name}{thr} ({side} implicit)
m.eld.one_per_side: '{a}' and '{b}': an item has only one {side} implicit
m.eld.conflict_two: an {orb} target together with another Eldritch target is not modelled: the Orb lowers the other implicit
m.step.eld.title: Eldritch implicit ({side})
m.step.eld.detail: Works on a Normal, Magic or Rare item and replaces only the {side} implicit: explicit mods and the other Eldritch implicit stay, and explicit currency never changes it, so this step costs the same whenever you do it (doing it first is simplest). Odds: tier {tier} pool, spawn weights from the game data. {note}
m.step.eld.fail: A different implicit (or a value below the threshold): apply another {cur} - it replaces the {side} implicit only.
m.frac.label: {label} (fractured)
m.frac.influenced: the {orb} 'Cannot be used on Influenced or Fractured items' (currency text) and this base has {list} influence
m.frac.with_influence: a fractured target together with an influenced target is not modelled: the {orb} cannot be used after the influence Exalt (currency text), and the reverse order is not modelled
m.frac.bench_only: only available as a bench craft; the game data does not say whether a {orb} can pick a crafted modifier - not supported
m.frac.only_one: {names}: only one modifier can be fractured (the {orb} 'Cannot be used on ... Fractured items')
m.frac.step1.title: Get the target onto a rare
m.frac.chosen: - the planner fractures the rarest target first
m.frac.step1.detail: Each attempt starts on a fresh base (base price not included).
m.frac.step1.divine: Then {divine} until its value meets the threshold (~{n:.1f} per attempt), before fracturing.
m.frac.step1.fail: {target} has not rolled yet: reroll again (nothing is fractured yet, so the base is unaffected).
m.frac.step2.action: Apply {orb}: it fractures one random modifier and locks it in place - it must be {target}.
m.frac.step2.detail: Needs a rare with at least 4 modifiers and no influence (currency text). Chance = the average of 1/(number of modifiers) over the items reached above. {note}
m.frac.step2.fail_restart: Another modifier was fractured: start over on a fresh base - a fractured modifier is permanent, so this base can no longer get {target} fractured (this is what the cost assumes; base price not included).
m.frac.step2.fail_keep: Alternative: keep the item and craft around the wrongly fractured modifier.
m.fx.MoreGemLevel: {fossil}: its added modifiers (game data 'added_mods') are assumed to join the normal pool at their own spawn weights, with the fossil's tag weights (gem x10) applied to them too - the data lists the added mods but not how they are weighted.
m.fx.AbyssSocket: {fossil}: 'Has 1 Abyssal Socket' is forced (game data 'forced_mods'); it is a suffix in the data and is assumed to count toward the usual 4-6 mod count, like an essence's guaranteed modifier.
m.fx.NoTagless: how 'No Tagless modifiers' is applied - it is only a description, the fossil's weights say nothing about modifiers without tags
m.fx.RandomModifier: the random weights it applies ('Random effects revealed when resonator is fully socketed') are not in the data
m.fx.CorruptEssence: which Corrupt Essence modifier it adds and how it is picked (essences.json has no corruption-only flag or per-modifier chance)
m.fx.Fracture: which modifier 'Fracture a random modifier' picks
m.fx.LuckyMods: how much 'High Level modifiers are more common' changes the weights, and the exact 'lucky' value rule
m.fx.BetterSellPrice: it only adds a vendor sell-price modifier ('Item sells for much more to vendors') - no stat a target can ask for
m.fx.CorruptedImplicit: it corrupts the item and adds a corrupted implicit - implicit targets are outside the planner, and a corrupted item cannot be crafted further
m.fx.unknown: the effect '{text}' is not described by any data the planner can use
m.fx.no_mod: it adds or forces no modifier of its own
m.feat.not_found: not found in the game data's fossil list
m.feat.beast_note: The game data export contains no Beastcrafting recipes - not which beasts a recipe needs, not its cost, not what it adds or rerolls. Some outcome modifiers exist in mods.json (the Aspect suffixes 'of Farrul', 'of Saqawal', 'of Fenumus', 'of Craiceann', with no spawn weights), but nothing links a recipe to them.

m.sp.forbidden_tags: the {fossil} cannot be used on items tagged {tags}

m.sp.with_other: a special-fossil target together with an influenced, veiled, Elevated or fractured target is not modelled
m.sp.slots: {n} {side} targets (special-fossil modifiers included), but an item holds at most {max}
m.range.dom_low: best case: the {orb} always upgrades the target's base modifier (100%) - the cost cannot be lower than this
m.range.dom_high: worst case: the target's base modifier is always the one removed (0%) - no upper bound
m.range.dom_mid: if uniform over the {n} influenced modifiers on the item ({p:.0%} per Orb): an assumption, not in the game data
m.range.conf_low: best case: every {orb} raises the target implicit ({needs}) and its value meets the threshold - the cost cannot be lower than this
m.range.conf_high: worst case: the target implicit is never raised - no upper bound
m.range.conf_mid: no defensible middle estimate for the {orb}: the data says the chance 'depends on its relative strength' but gives no formula
m.range.text: {low:,.1f} c - no upper bound{mid} (odds unknown, see note)
m.range.note: Odds for {mech} are not in the game data. This plan shows a range, not a single number; treat it as a schematic, not a quote.
m.dom.label: {name}{thr} (Elevated {inf})
m.dom.no_pool: not supported (missing outcome data): the game data has no Elevated modifiers
m.dom.no_mod: no Elevated {inf} modifier with this stat line in the game data
m.dom.no_influence: needs an item with {inf} influence (pass the influence); getting the influence first with an Exalt and then using the {orb} is not modelled
m.dom.no_link: not supported (missing outcome data): no influenced modifier in the game data links to this Elevated modifier (same influence, side, group and stats)
m.dom.base_not_on: its base modifier does not roll on {base} with {inf} influence
m.dom.top_ilvl: the highest tier of its base modifier needs item level {lvl} (only a highest-tier modifier becomes Elevated)
m.dom.below: the Elevated modifier reaches {top:g}, below the threshold
m.dom.two: more than one Elevated target: each {orb} removes an influenced modifier, so a second one is not modelled
m.dom.with_other: an Elevated target together with an influenced, veiled or fractured target is not modelled
m.dom.influenced_target: '{label}' is an influenced modifier: the {orb} could remove it, which is not modelled - keep only the Elevated target among influenced modifiers
m.dom.slots: {n} explicit {side} targets plus the Elevated modifier's base, but an item holds at most {max}
m.dom.step.action: Check the item has exactly 2 influenced modifiers ({base} and {sac}), then apply the {orb}: it must remove the sacrificed one and upgrade the highest-tier one into {label}.
m.dom.step.chance: unknown - best case 100% (target always upgraded), {p:.0%} if uniform over the {n} influenced modifiers (assumption), worst case 0% (target always removed)
m.dom.step.fail_redo: The {orb} removed the target's base modifier and upgraded the other one: redo the preparation above (what the range assumes; re-adding only that modifier is not modelled).
m.dom.step.fail_more: More than 2 influenced modifiers on the item: the uniform figure would be 1 in their number - not computed.
m.dom.pass_note: Cost here is one preparation pass; a failed {orb} repeats it (see the range).
m.conf.no_t3: not supported (missing outcome data): the {orb} route needs the Exceptional (tier 3) version of this implicit on this base, and the data has none
m.conf.no_lesser: the {orb} needs a {side} implicit too, and no Lesser currency for it applies to {cls}
m.conf.t3.title: Eldritch implicit ({side}), tier 3
m.conf.t3.detail: Tier 3 is the highest an Ember/Ichor creates; the {orb} raises it from there. {note}
m.conf.other.action: Apply one {cur}: any {other} implicit will do (the {orb} needs both sides).
m.conf.orb.action: Apply the {orb}: it must raise the {side} implicit to tier 2{then}.
m.conf.orb.detail: {range_note} Best case (lower bound): every Orb raises the target - {n} Orb(s) of Conflict and {n} {cur} (a lowered Lesser implicit is removed and must be re-added). Worst case: never raised - no upper bound. {note}
m.conf.orb.chance: unknown - the data says the chance 'depends on its relative strength' but gives no odds; best case 100% per Orb, worst case 0%
m.conf.orb.fail_raised: The {other} implicit was raised and the target lowered: more Orbs of Conflict - not computed (no upper bound).
m.conf.orb.fail_removed: The {other} implicit was Lesser and got removed: apply another {cur} before the next Orb (counted in the best case).
m.vl.label: {name}{thr} (Veiled)
m.vl.not_unveiled: not an unveiled modifier in the game data
m.vl.member: only unveiled from a Syndicate member's own veiled modifier ({members}); {aisling} and the {vc} give the generic pool - not supported
m.vl.not_pool: not in the unveil pool of {cls} ({base}): the spawn weights of this unveiled modifier exclude every tag of this base
m.vl.ilvl: needs item level {lvl}+ (required level of the unveiled modifier)
m.vl.below: the unveiled modifier reaches {top:g} here, below the threshold
m.vl.two: more than one veiled target: an item holds one veiled modifier at a time, and unveiling several in sequence is not modelled
m.vl.with_other: a veiled target together with a fractured or influenced target is not modelled
m.vl.group: '{a}' and '{b}' cannot be on the same item: both belong to the mod group {groups}, and an item holds one mod per group
m.vl.slots: {n} explicit {side} targets plus the veiled {side}, but an item holds at most {max} {side}es
m.vl.repeat_chaos: The chance shown is for the other targets; with the veiled modifier on the {side} side and the unveil hit, ~{f:.1f} times as many rerolls are needed.
m.vl.repeat_aisling_restart: With the Aisling finish this part repeats ~{f:.2f} times per finished item on average (restart).
m.vl.repeat_aisling_annul: With the Aisling finish this part repeats ~{f:.2f} times per finished item on average (only when an Annulment removes a target).
m.vl.fail_reroll: Target not offered: unveil any option and {vc} again (this is what the cost assumes).
m.vl.fail_recovery: Annul / metacraft recovery to keep this item instead: not computed for Veiled Chaos plans.
m.vl.side_extra: The veiled modifier must be a {side}: {p:.0%} assumed (not in the data); per {vc} that has the other targets, {finish} finish.
m.vl.unveil.title: Unveil (Jun)
m.vl.unveil.action: Unveil the veiled {side} and choose {target} from the {k} options.
m.vl.unveil.detail: {pool} possible {side} outcomes on this base; chance that one of the {k} options is {label}: {p}.{extra} {note}
m.vl.unveil.state: Rare with {target} (an ordinary explicit modifier from now on)
m.vl.br.restart: Start over on a fresh base: {cost:,.1f} c per finished item for the rolling + Aisling part{tail}
m.vl.br.annul: {annul} until it removes the wrong unveiled modifier (1 in {n}; removing a target means starting over), then Aisling again: {cost:,.1f} c per finished item for the rolling + Aisling part{tail} Approximate: other random mods on the item are ignored.
m.vl.br.lock: Protect the other side with a 'Cannot Be Changed' metacraft before annulling: not computed.
m.vl.ais.action: Aisling in Research (rank 3): adds a veiled modifier, which must take the free {side} slot.
m.vl.ais.annul: The cost includes the {annul} retries after a wrong unveil.
m.vl.ais.chance: 100% (assumed - Aisling is not in the game data)
m.inf.label: {name}{thr} ({inf} influence)
m.inf.with_eldritch: cannot be combined with an Eldritch implicit target: Embers and Ichors 'Cannot be used on Shaper, Elder or Elderslayer influenced items' (currency text), and whether an influence Exalt may follow an Eldritch implicit is not stated in the game data - not supported
m.inf.preinfluenced: an influence Exalted Orb needs 'a rare item with no influence' and this base already has {list} influence; combining a pre-influenced base with Awakener's Orb is not modelled
m.inf.same_twice: '{a}' and '{b}': an influence Exalt adds one {inf} modifier; a second {inf} modifier would have to roll on the influenced item, which is not modelled
m.inf.too_many: {n} influences targeted ({list}), but an item can have at most two (Awakener's Orb combines two)
m.slots.affix: {n} {side} targets, but an item holds at most {max} {side}es
m.inf.no_influence_needed: this stat line rolls on {base} without any influence - drop '({inf})'
m.inf.other_influence: on {cls} this is a {others} modifier, not a {inf} modifier
m.inf.ilvl: requires item level {lvl} (this base is item level {ilvl})
m.inf.no_mod: {cls} has no {inf} modifier with this stat line (the influence's spawn weights exclude it)
m.inf.below: the highest {inf} tier on this base reaches {top:g}, below the threshold
m.inf.step.action: Apply {exalt} to the rare item (it must have no influence): it adds {inf} influence and one {inf} modifier, which must be {target}.
m.inf.step.detail: {pct:.3g}% of the {pool} {inf} modifiers' spawn weight on this base. {note}
m.inf.step.fail_restart: A different {inf} modifier: start over from 'Get the base' with a fresh base (the influence cannot be removed; this is what the cost assumes, base price not included).
m.inf.step.fail_annul: Alternative: Orb of Annulment on the wrong influenced modifier, then regular Exalted Orbs - the item keeps its influence, so its modifiers can roll.
m.aw.bases.title: Get two bases
m.aw.bases.action: Two {base} (item level {ilvl}+), Normal or Rare, without influence - one becomes the donor, the other the item you keep.
m.aw.bases.detail: Base items are not priced anywhere in the planner.
m.aw.item.title: {role}: {inf} item
m.aw.item.action: Craft a {base} with {inf} influence and exactly one {inf} modifier: {target}. Cheapest computed route: {route}.
m.aw.item.detail: Buying one instead is not priced (the price data has currency, not items). {note}
m.aw.item.fail: Wrong influenced modifier: start that item over on a fresh base (an influence Exalted Orb needs an item without influence, so this one cannot try again).
m.aw.orb.action: Apply {orb}: click the donor first (it is destroyed), then the second item - it is reforged as a rare with both influences and new modifiers.
m.aw.orb.detail_rest: The other targets ({rest}) must appear in the reforge; odds from the dual-influence modifier pool.
m.aw.orb.fail_restart: The reforge kept both influenced targets but not the other targets: start over with a new donor and second item (this is what the cost assumes).
m.aw.orb.fail_alt: Alternative: Exalted Orbs / Annulment on the dual-influenced item.
m.feas.below: the highest tier available here reaches {top:g}, below the threshold
m.feas.group: '{a}' and '{b}' cannot be on the same item: every mod that gives them belongs to the mod group {groups}, and an item holds one mod per group
m.why.no_mod: no mod with this stat line exists in the game data
m.why.needs_influence: requires {list} influence, which this item does not have{full}{hint}
m.why.hint: - mark the target '({inf})' to craft it with the {exalt}
m.why.ilvl: requires item level {lvl} (this base is item level {ilvl})
m.why.nothing: cannot appear on {cls} ({base}) through any supported method
m.rec.too_large: Annul/metacraft recovery not computed for this plan: {error} (state space too large).
m.rec.never_cheaper: Annul / metacraft recovery was computed for this plan and is never cheaper than rerolling here.
m.rec.policy_note: Recovery policy computed by value iteration over the same item states as the reroll odds (non-target mods use the same per-affix aggregation).
m.sim.low_conf: only {n:,} simulated attempts (target {target:,}); 95% CI width {width:.3g} percentage points
m.pol.restart: {p} of attempts: no target mod rolled - {then}.
m.pol.action: {p} of attempts: {label} - these items are worth keeping: on average this saves ~{save:,.1f} c compared with starting over (finishes without starting over {f:.0%} of the time - see the recovery steps below).
m.recstep.title: Recovery: {what}
m.recstep.detail: Used only in the item states where the computed policy picks it; uses and cost are per finished item.{extra}
m.recstep.chance: {p} of uses move the item closer to the targets
m.recstep.success: Re-evaluate the item and take the next policy step.
m.recfail.annul: The Annulment removed a target mod instead of the unwanted one{meta}: the policy continues from the new item - Exalt the missing target back, Annul again, or start over when keeping the item would cost more than starting over.
m.recfail.slam: The Exalted Orb added a non-target mod: the policy continues from the new item - Annul it, Exalt again, or start over when keeping the item would cost more than starting over.
m.recfail.scour: Scouring under the lock is deterministic (only the unlocked side is wiped): the policy continues from the new item - Exalt the missing targets, or start over when keeping the item would cost more than starting over.
m.recfail.chaos: The Chaos Orb rerolled the unlocked side without the missing targets: the policy continues from the new item - Annul, Exalt, another locked reroll, or start over when keeping the item would cost more than starting over.
m.reroll.modcount: Odds assume the standard rare mod-count distribution (4/5/6 mods = 8/12, 3/12, 1/12; not published by GGG).
m.recref: Instead of starting over, the computed Annul/metacraft recovery policy brings this plan to ~{cost:,.1f} c (see '{name} + Annul/metacraft recovery').
m.base.title: Get the base
m.base.detail: Higher item level unlocks higher tiers; tiers above your item level cannot roll.
m.done.title: Done
m.extra.multimod: room for Multimod + both bench crafts
m.extra.influence: free {side} and no influence, for the {exalt}
m.alch.title: Make it rare
m.reroll.harvest: Harvest 'Reforge a Rare item with new random modifiers, including a {label} modifier'
m.reroll.again_scour: {scour} first, then repeat this step: this essence tier only upgrades a Normal item ('Upgrades a normal item to rare'), and Scouring turns the failed rare back into a Normal one
m.reroll.essence: Guaranteed: {mod}. The other mods roll like a {chaos}.
m.reroll.title: Reroll: {what}
m.reroll.action_policy: Apply {what}; then follow the computed policy.
m.reroll.chance_policy: {direct} hit directly; {finish} of attempts finish (directly or after recovery)
m.reroll.missing: Not every target rolled: {again} - a reroll replaces all modifiers, including target mods that did roll.
m.reroll.chance_inner: {p} per attempt; tries and cost below are per finished item
m.magic.title: Make it magic
m.alt.title: Alteration spam
m.alt.fail_aug: Exactly one target mod and an empty opposite slot: {aug} (happens on {p} of Alterations; included in the odds).
m.alt.fail_again: Otherwise (the magic item is missing a target): {alt} again - it rerolls the magic item's modifiers.
m.regal.chance: {p} to add a missing target directly
m.regal.restart: {scour} (the rare item becomes Normal again) and go back to 'Make it magic'
m.chain.fail: The added modifier is not the target: {scour} (the rare item becomes Normal again) and go back to 'Make it magic' (this is what the cost assumes).
m.mm.both: If both are missing ({p} of finished rolls): craft 'Can have up to 3 Crafted Modifiers' ({cost:g}c), then '{a}' and '{b}'. If one of them rolled naturally, craft only the other (no Multimod needed).
m.mm.either: Craft whichever is missing: '{a}' or '{b}'. The reroll step only accepts items where one of them rolled naturally, because both crafts plus Multimod would not fit in the free slots.
m.bench.title: Crafting bench
m.mm.detail: Multimod occupies a suffix slot; the reroll odds above already reserve it when needed. Value re-crafts are included in the cost.{extra}
m.bench.value: . Value >= threshold on {p} of crafts; re-craft via 'Remove crafted mods' otherwise.
m.divine.action: {divine} until every value meets its threshold.
m.divine.detail_low: Tiers that can reach your thresholds were accepted earlier; this rerolls the numbers. If this is expensive, lower the thresholds.
m.divine.detail: Tiers that can reach your thresholds were accepted earlier; this rerolls the numbers.
m.inf.repeat: With the final {exalt} this whole part repeats on a fresh base ~{n:.1f} times on average (once per Exalt attempt).
m.act.lock_annul: Bench '{meta}' → {annul} (only {other}es can go) → remove crafted mods
m.rec.err_eldritch: Recovery mode works on explicit mods only; Eldritch implicits are not modelled in recovery. Remove the Eldritch target for --have and plan the implicit separately with `plan` (Embers/Ichors never touch explicit mods, so the two can be done independently).
m.rec.err_veiled: Recovery mode works on explicit mods only; a veiled target is not modelled in recovery. Use `plan` for the veiled target (Aisling or Veiled Chaos Orb, then unveil).
m.rec.err_mod: Unknown mod id '{mid}' (list them with `python -m poecraft mods --base ... --tiers`)
m.rec.err_count: An item cannot hold more than {n} {side}es
m.rec.err_group: Two of the given mods share a mod group - an item cannot have both
m.rec.err_large: The recovery state space is too large to compute for this item.
m.rec.current.title: Current item
m.rec.finish_bench: (includes the bench craft '{mod}'; optional Divine Orbs not included)
m.rec.finish.title: Finish
m.rec.finish.action: Targets already present: finish with the bench craft / Divine.
m.rec.restart.title: Start over
m.rec.restart.action: Keeping this item costs more than starting over ({state}): {start}.
m.rec.restart.detail: Every recovery action was computed and is more expensive than starting over.
m.rec.option.detail: Keeps every target mod already on the item {p} of the time.{finish}
m.rec.option.finish: Finishing this item without ever starting over: ~{cost:,.1f} c.
m.rec.continue.title: Continue with the computed policy
m.rec.continue.action: After every step take the action the policy assigns to the new item (Exalt, Annul, metacraft, or start over).
m.rec.continue.detail: Expected cost from the new item{finish}.
m.rec.continue.fail: If the policy gives up: {start} (~{cost:,.1f} c).
m.inf.no_combo: Every target is reachable on its own, but no supported strategy produces all of them on one item (e.g. they need different essences, or no free slot remains for the bench craft).
m.sel.range_demoted: range-based, worst case exceeds the best deterministic plan ({why})
m.ctx.not_on_base: Mod '{label}' cannot appear on {base} (item level {ilvl}, influences {inf})
m.srv.expired: This plan is no longer in memory (the server keeps the last 16) - build it again to change its language.
m.ctx.too_many: {n} {side} targets requested, an item can only hold {max}

m.sim.timeout: simulation stopped at the {secs:g} s time limit after {n:,} of {target:,} runs - low confidence (timeout)
m.sim.phase_skipped: Not simulated: the simulation phase used its {secs:g} s time limit before reaching this strategy; its numbers are the fast calculation only.
m.warn.sim_timeout: Simulation timed out. Results are approximate: the simulation of {names} stopped at the {secs:g} s limit (the fast calculation is complete; only its check is shorter).
m.warn.sim_skipped: Simulation timed out. Results are approximate: the simulation phase reached its {secs:g} s limit, so {names} were not simulated.
m.rec.time_limit: Recovery via Annul/metacraft was not computed for this plan: solving its policy ran past the time limit ({secs:g} s per variant, {total:g} s per plan).

m.divine.optional_note: Optional and not in the expected cost: without it, every value already meets its threshold on {p} of finished items; otherwise the tiers are right and only the numbers are short.
m.pol.restart_guaranteed: {p} of attempts: the guaranteed mod {mod} is there, but the rest is not worth working on - {then}. The essence puts {mod} back with every reforge, and at {per:.1f} c per try that is cheaper here than adding the missing targets with {exalt} / {annul} (the recovery policy compared both in every item state).
m.pol.restart_partial: {p} of attempts: not worth finishing - {then}. {q} of these items do have target mods, but adding the missing ones with {exalt} / {annul} costs more here than another try (the recovery policy compared both in every item state).
m.pol.restart_fractured: {p} of attempts: the fractured mod {mod} stays, but the rest is not worth working on - {then}. A reroll never removes a fractured modifier, and here another try is cheaper than adding the missing targets with {exalt} / {annul} (the recovery policy compared both in every item state).

hub.tool.evaluator.title: Item Evaluator
hub.tool.evaluator.desc: Price-check any item on the trade site in the current league: online sellers first, cheapest first. For rares, the search relaxes what matters least until it finds comparable items.
eval.placeholder: Hover an item in game, press Ctrl+C (or Ctrl+Alt+C), paste here.
eval.hint: Searches the official trade site in the current league, online sellers first.
eval.busy: Searching the trade site… this can take 10–30 s: the trade site limits how often it may be asked.
eval.cached: cached result, up to 5 min old
eval.rankingHint: Ranked by how hard each property is to get. When nothing is found, the cheapest-to-recreate ones are dropped first; the core is always kept.
eval.open: Open this search on the trade site
m.imp.approx: Matched approximately: '{line}' read as the game's '{match}'
m.imp.eld_side: '{line}': the item says {said}, but in the game data this implicit belongs to {data} - using {data}
m.imp.not_on_base_defence: {base} has only {has}, but '{line}' needs {needs}: this base cannot have it (skipped). Check the copied text - the base name or this line may be wrong.
m.imp.base_defence_mismatch: The item's defence lines ({lines}) do not match {base} ({has}): the base name or the properties may be miscopied.
eval.summary.offline: No online sellers - offline listings only
m.eval.timeless_unread: This looks like a Timeless Jewel, but its seed line ("Commanded leadership over … warriors under …") is missing from the text - copy the jewel again with Ctrl+C.
m.eval.timeless_no_data: The Timeless Jewel data is not downloaded yet, so the effects cannot be calculated (run `python -m poecraft timeless update`). The trade listings below still work.
m.eval.timeless_seed: Seed {seed} is outside this jewel's range ({lo}-{hi}): the text may be miscopied.
eval.tj.title: Timeless Jewel calculator
eval.tj.pick: Choose the socket - in the list or on the tree
eval.tj.namesNote: Passive names and stats are shown in English (the passive tree export is English only).

eval.tj.trade: This exact jewel on the trade site
m.eval.type_only: Searched by base type ({base}): {what} aren't filtered automatically - use the base search below.
m.tradeerr.no_id: the trade site returned no search id
m.tradeerr.slot: trade site request limit: the next search frees in {s} s - try again then
m.imp.corrupted: Corrupted item: it cannot be changed any more - the plan is for crafting a fresh base like it.
m.imp.mirrored: Mirrored item: it cannot be changed - the plan is for crafting a fresh base like it.
m.imp.not_craftable_currency: This is currency, not something to craft: {lines}. The Item Evaluator prices it.
m.imp.not_craftable_divination: This is a divination card, not something to craft: {lines}. The Item Evaluator prices it.
m.imp.not_craftable_gem: This is a gem, not something to craft: {lines}. The Item Evaluator prices it.
m.imp.not_craftable_unique: This unique's base is not a craftable base: {lines}. The Item Evaluator prices it by name.
m.srv.internal: Something went wrong on the server (it has been logged). Please try again.
m.eval.none_found: Nothing listed on the trade site in this league, offline sellers included.
m.rec.restart_unfractured: "Start over" is priced as rolling the fractured modifier again (a fresh fractured base with this influence cannot be planned); Scouring keeps a fractured modifier, so the real restart is cheaper.
m.imp.eld_unlisted: Eldritch implicit not listed for this base in the game data: '{line}' - the price search uses it as written (the planner cannot plan it). If the item is not what it says, check the copied text.
m.eval.why.eld_unlisted: Eldritch implicit (not in the data for this base): importance unknown
eval.tj.equivHint: Tick the notables you need: other seeds that change them the same way (or with higher rolls) are priced too. Fewer ticks find more seeds.
eval.tj.equivBusy: Comparing every seed and pricing the equivalents on the trade site…
eval.tj.equivFound: {exact} of {n} other seeds change the must-have notables the same way (or better). The cheapest {scanned} listings of this jewel and conqueror were checked, plus a search by seed - cheapest first.
eval.tj.equivClosest: No other seed among {n} matches every must-have notable - these come closest. Untick some to find exact equivalents.
eval.tj.equivNone: No other seed among {n} changes any must-have notable the same way.
